Latin word

dīmittō

dīmittō, dīmittere, dīmīsī, dīmissum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

dismiss, let go, discharge; forgive (a debt, a sin); let go of, release

In this lexicon

  • fire

    the recommended word · classical · Suet. Aug. 24.2: cum ignōminiā tōtam dīmīsit; Traupman 305: dismiss, dīmittō; Traupman 305

  • forgive

    also used · late Latin · Vulg. Mt. 6.12; Vulg. Mt. 18.21

  • let go

    the recommended word · classical

  • per aetheris undās dīmittō: broadcast

    modern

Examples

  • decimam legiōnem contumācius pārentem cum ignōminiā tōtam dīmīsit, item aliās immodestē missiōnem postulantēs citrā commoda ēmeritōrum praemiōrum exauctōrāvit

    the tenth legion, which obeyed with insolence, he dismissed in disgrace to a man, and others who demanded their discharge rudely he discharged without the rewards due for completed serviceSuet. Aug. 24.2

    In the entry for fire
